Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International: the custom footprint's 21 block-group weight_share values are land/property-area shares of the official airport boundary, and corr(weight_share, block-group land area) = 0.88. Unlike the Harvard case the mass is not misplaced: the airport-property block group 130639800001 (0 residents) takes 69.9% of the mass, and those receiving block groups hold 0 residents (0-46 residents across the four audited airport footprints), so the counts land on the airport property where the incidents actually happen. What is meaningless is the implied RATE, not the location: a resident denominator of 0-46 people cannot express airport crime, and the index is suppressed on those block groups anyway, so no published value depends on the weights. Reweighting to an activity basis would move the counts nowhere useful - there is no resident or worker population inside an airfield to reweight toward, and the airport property IS the agency's jurisdiction. Footprint rows left untouched.

source_note: Official HUPD Clery and operational sources show MA0096200 follows Harvard owned or controlled Massachusetts campuses and affiliated residences across Cambridge Allston Boston Somerville Bedford and Petersham rather than a single place or county proxy.
reviewer_note: S2-6b rebuilt. OLD weight basis: a Harvard/MassGIS parcel-envelope hybrid whose 56 block-group weight_share values correlated 0.885 with block-group land area and near zero with activity, so 69.8% of HUPD mass (about 408 of 584 counts) landed on block group 250277042021, the Petersham/Harvard Forest block group about 65 miles from campus, at an implied 34,144 per 100k. NEW weight basis: LandScan USA 2021 DAYTIME population (residents+workers+students+shoppers) inside property-x-block-group over TIGER 2020 MA area landmarks for Harvard (K2540 "Harvard Univ", "Harvard Medical Schl", "Harvard Forest-Harvard Univ") plus the Arnold Arboretum (K2180) plus the containing 2020 census block of the one HUPD-scope property no landmark polygon reaches (Concord Field Station, Bedford); native 3-arcsecond cell-center rasterization, the same extraction that reproduces the published UC Berkeley CA0019700 weights exactly. Footprint is now 29 block groups. Mass moves to the actual campuses: Allston/Harvard Business School 250250008062 0.1792, Cambridge campus core 250173537003 0.1770 and 250173537005 0.1341, Harvard Yard/Law School 250173536002 0.1157, Longwood/Harvard Medical School 250250810015 0.1070. HARVARD FOREST: block group 250277042021 is KEPT but drops from 0.698082 to 0.000214 (13 modelled daytime people inside the forest polygon, about 0.13 of 584 counts instead of 408); the rural Concord/Carlisle Harvard woodland block group 250173613005 falls out entirely from 0.126607 because it has no modelled daytime population. Peak implied rate falls from 34,144 per 100k in Petersham to about 11,400 per 100k on the Longwood block group, which is a genuine low-resident high-daytime campus block rather than a misplacement. displaces_county_remainder left empty: a university police force is a concurrent overlap, not the primary agency.

source_note: Official MAA and MDTA sources tie MD0020300 to the bounded BWI airport-property and operational-facilities footprint rather than any county place or statewide MDTA proxy.
reviewer_note: S2-6b ACCEPTED AS BENIGN - deliberately NOT changed. BWI Thurgood Marshall (Maryland Aviation Administration): the custom footprint's 8 block-group weight_share values are land/property-area shares of the official airport boundary, and corr(weight_share, block-group land area) = 0.42. Unlike the Harvard case the mass is not misplaced: the airport-property block group 240039800001 (0 residents) takes 79.7% of the mass, and those receiving block groups hold 0 residents (0-46 residents across the four audited airport footprints), so the counts land on the airport property where the incidents actually happen. What is meaningless is the implied RATE, not the location: a resident denominator of 0-46 people cannot express airport crime, and the index is suppressed on those block groups anyway, so no published value depends on the weights. Reweighting to an activity basis would move the counts nowhere useful - there is no resident or worker population inside an airfield to reweight toward, and the airport property IS the agency's jurisdiction. Footprint rows left untouched.
